overview: The School Committee heard presentations on the middle school Canoe Mobile program, strategic plan survey results, and Medford High School's late bus service. The Committee also discussed a proposed policy to regulate and prioritize elementary school reassignment requests, taking no action to allow for further revisions.

items.title: Consent Agenda
items.summary: Approved the consent agenda, including bills and payrolls, a $295,000 Beth Israel Leahy Health grant, a gas donation to Brooks Elementary School, and minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: Mustang Moment: Canoe Mobile Program
items.summary: Principal Nick Tucci and sixth-grade students Adelaide and B Strassfeld shared their experiences participating in the Canoe Mobile outdoor education program on the Mystic River.

items.title: Strategic Plan Survey Results and Process Update
items.summary: Member Jessica Parks presented results from the district's strategic plan survey, and Superintendent Suzanne Galusi provided an update on the first phase of the strategic planning process being conducted with Lynch Leadership Academy.

items.title: Student Advisory Council: Medford High School Late Bus
items.summary: Student representatives Ryan Threat and William Barabinha presented on the newly introduced high school late bus service, highlighting its role in expanding access to after-school activities.

items.title: Resolution 2026-24: Elementary School Reassignment Policy
items.summary: The Committee discussed a proposed policy to formalize guidelines, timelines, and enrollment buffers for alternative elementary school placements. No vote was taken, as the policy was held for further refinement based on committee feedback.
